title: The Mỹ Cảnh floating restaurant is bombed
description: On the evening of 25 June 1965 the Viet Cong bombed the Mỹ Cảnh, the floating restaurant on the Saigon River where Larry and Ron Tototz always ate. Larry says he was in front of it when a friend named Lopez — a Marine, his pal from the cub scouts — showed up and invited him to the Peacock instead, and when they walked into the Peacock the Mỹ Cảnh blew up. "It was like a guardian angel." He describes the weapon as a claymore mine that "fires 700 buckshot bullets in a curve." The next day, he says, he took pictures of the wreck; those pictures are not in the collection. The date of the bombing is documented; that Larry was there is his account.
researchNotes: The bombing is documented: two command-detonated mines, 44 dead including 13 Americans (frus-1964-68-v03-d20, cited, written the next morning; it says nothing about Larry). His account came unasked on 2026-09-05 at VN-0068 (giscus-vn-0068-c18307841, transcribed), with VN-0072, VN-0079 and VN-0089 the same sitting. It is the only day of his tour he fixes to a documented date by being there: in Saigon on 25 June 1965, sixteen days after Đồng Xoài, which he says he heard from the mountain. Nothing documentary places him at the restaurant, and the next-day photographs were never scanned (research/photos/scan-reconciliation-2026-09-01.md). 2026-09-14: the search hypothesis for Lopez and a statement about which bombing VN-0120 belongs to were removed from this note. The Lopez hypothesis stays in research/events/my-canh-bombing-1965.md (ledger #32, issue #128) and must not reach a page. VN-0120 against the Embassy and the Market is open (research/events/saigon-market-bombing.md, ledger #23, #36) and is not stated here. Ledger #30, issue #127.
